Setting up Hasura for WebVox

Configure Hasura to expose a secure GraphQL endpoint over your SQL database for WebVox intent orchestration.

Overview

WebVox relies on a Data Abstraction Layer to automatically generate a GraphQL API over your schema. By connecting Hasura, WebVox can query your existing databases through a unified, secure endpoint while enforcing row and column-level permissions.

Prerequisites

  • A running SQL database (PostgreSQL, MySQL, etc.).
  • Connection details (host, port, DB name, username, password).
  • Access to create a Hasura project.
1

Deploy Hasura

Create a new project using Hasura Cloud (recommended) or deploy via Docker/Kubernetes. Once running, open the Hasura console in your browser.

2

Connect Your Database

Navigate to Data → Connect Database. Choose your database type, enter your connection string, and verify. Hasura will introspect your schema automatically.

3

Track Tables & Relationships

In the connected database view, mark the tables you want WebVox to access as "Tracked". Define relationships (object/array) so queries can traverse your data graph.

Pro Tip: Rename fields to align with natural domain language. The WebVox query planner uses this metadata to map natural language intents to GraphQL!
4

Configure Security & Permissions

Under the Permissions tab for each tracked table, define roles (e.g., anonymous, user). Configure allowed operations (Select/Insert) and apply row/column-level filters. WebVox strictly respects these permissions.

5

Enable the GraphQL Endpoint

Hasura generates a single endpoint (e.g., /v1/graphql). Copy this URL and your admin/role-based authentication method (like JWT).

6

Test Your Connection

Use the Hasura GraphiQL console to run a simple query. Verify that the expected data is returned and permissions behave correctly based on the applied roles.
